findings.description: Critical: D7 says the router upserts a `pending_gates` entry 'keyed by `decision_id`' through `cycle_state.write_mirror`, and supervise.Supervise Gate Routing scenario 11 plus Supervisor Rehydration Record 'Pending gate carries the deadline' assert the rehydrated entry carries `decision_id`. But `cycle_state._clean_pending_gate` (skills/supervise/scripts/cycle_state.py:229-257) is a strict allowlist: it rebuilds the entry from `gate`, `change_id`, `requested_at`, `deadline`, `disposition`, `approval_id`, `source` and silently drops every other key. `write_mirror` runs each entry through `_durable_sections` -> `_clean_pending_gate`, so `decision_id` is stripped on write and the projection key never survives to a rehydrated session. No task edits `_clean_pending_gate`: task 1.3 only grows the schemas, task 2.2 only writes the router, and task 2.8 only swaps the `_GATES`/`_DISPOSITIONS` literals for enum imports.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit task under wp-router (paired with the 2.8 enum swap, same file) to teach `cycle_state._clean_pending_gate` to carry `decision_id` (validated as a uuid4 string), and name the change in D7 and in the task 2.1 test list. Note that `skills/supervise/scripts/cycle_state.py` is already inside wp-router's `write_allow` and lock set, so only the task and design text are missing.

findings.description: Critical: the roadmap-orchestration delta rewrites 'Preserve a parked child' to say the parked metadata '(gate, deadline, any filed `approval_id`)' stays available to the gate router, but a filed `approval_id` cannot exist there. `openspec/contracts/roadmap-orchestration/schemas/supervised-dispatch-result.schema.json` defines `parked` as `additionalProperties: false` over exactly `{kind, reason, gate, deadline, resume_hint}`, and `skills/supervise/scripts/execution.py:416` independently rejects any key outside that same set. design.md Context states the same fact in the opposite direction ('never an `approval_id`'), which is what D4's prior-record rule was rewritten around in iteration 1. The delta therefore asserts a contract-forbidden field and contradicts its own design.
findings.resolution: Drop `any filed approval_id` from the 'Preserve a parked child' scenario in specs/roadmap-orchestration/spec.md; say the parked snapshot carries the gate and deadline and that the filed-approval state lives in the router's own ledger (D4 step 0.3), not in the child result.

findings.description: Critical: the plan never says where the roadmap workspace's `checkpoint.json` comes from for the `cycle` gate. `gate_router.evaluate` records through `CheckpointManager.record_gate_decision` (skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/checkpoint.py:98), which calls `save()` on a `Checkpoint` the caller must first `load()` — and `CheckpointManager.load()` raises `FileNotFoundError` when `checkpoint.json` is absent (checkpoint.py:44-53). Nine of the ten workspaces under `openspec/roadmaps/` have no `checkpoint.json`; only `roadmap-supervisor-orchestration` does, because it has been executed. `orchestrator.py:178` is the only bootstrap (`manager.load() if manager.exists() else manager.create(roadmap)`), and it runs inside `execute`, i.e. after D5 has `gate-check` evaluate `roadmap_approval` at the end of the digest. A first `cycle` on any un-executed roadmap therefore crashes in the router instead of parking the gate.
findings.resolution: State in D5 which component creates the checkpoint for a first `gate-check` (either the router bootstraps with `CheckpointManager.create(roadmap)` like the orchestrator does, or `gate-check` writes to a gate-only sidecar until execution creates the checkpoint), add the choice to task 2.2, and add a `gate-check` / `gate-log` on a workspace with no checkpoint case to the task 2.7 test list.

findings.description: Critical: D6 claims `gate-log` makes 'every gate raised during a supervised run answerable from tracked state' by unioning the checkpoint sidecar with `openspec/changes/<change_id>/loop-state.json` for each of the roadmap's items. `loop-state.json` is neither tracked nor present in the supervisor's checkout: `git ls-files openspec/changes` returns loop-state files only under `archive/`, and the live file for this very change does not exist in a second worktree of the same branch. A child's loop state lives in that child's isolated worktree (`attempt.isolation.worktree_path`; the result carries `evidence.loop_state_path`). So `gate-log --roadmap R` run from the supervisor's repo root finds zero records for every in-flight child, and acceptance outcome 2 is unmet for exactly the seven autopilot gates that produce most decisions. The task 2.10 e2e fitness function cannot catch it because it co-locates everything in one tmp workspace.
findings.resolution: Change D6 to resolve each item's loop state through the attempt's recorded `isolation.worktree_path` / `evidence.loop_state_path` rather than the supervisor's `openspec/changes/<change_id>/`, falling back to the supervisor path only for a merged change, and report unreadable child state as a degraded origin instead of silence. Update task 2.10 to place at least one child's loop-state outside the supervisor repo root so the test can fail.

findings.description: Critical: task 2.6 adds the `^gate-decision:<uuid4>$` pattern to `continuation.approval_ref` in `openspec/contracts/roadmap-orchestration/schemas/delegated-dispatch-attempt.schema.json`, but `skills/tests/autopilot-roadmap/test_supervised_dispatch.py:483` writes `continuation={"kind": "pending_gate", "approval_ref": "approval-1"}` into a checkpoint that `apply_delegated_batch` then validates. That literal stops matching the new pattern, so wp-router's own second verification step (`cd skills && uv run pytest tests/roadmap-runtime tests/autopilot-roadmap -q`) fails — and `skills/tests/autopilot-roadmap/**` is in no package's `write_allow` except wp-integration's, which runs after. wp-router cannot make its own gate green.
findings.resolution: Add `skills/tests/autopilot-roadmap/test_supervised_dispatch.py` to wp-router's `scope.write_allow` and lock set, and name the fixture update in task 2.6 (or task 2.5's migration list). Also note that `skills/tests/supervise/fixtures/execution/contracts/invalid-continuation-without-kind.json` will become invalid for two reasons once the pattern lands, which weakens that fixture's assertion.

findings.description: Critical: the Risks table and task 3.2 mitigate `test_workflow_contract.py` by keeping two headings and the phrase ``durable `approval_ref` ``, but `test_execute_requires_one_durable_roadmap_altitude_approval_before_mutation` (skills/tests/supervise/test_workflow_contract.py:29-37) pins six phrases inside `### Approval gate`, including `before any roadmap checkpoint or execution-state mutation`. Under this design `execute` opens with `gate-check`, which appends a gate-decision record to `openspec/roadmaps/<id>/checkpoint.json` before any approval exists — so that assertion becomes false, not merely at risk. The plan currently reads as if the section can be rewritten while every existing pin survives.
findings.resolution: Enumerate all six pinned phrases in the task 3.2 description, state that `before any roadmap checkpoint or execution-state mutation` must be replaced (the gate ledger write is the one checkpoint mutation that legitimately precedes approval), and say explicitly that `test_workflow_contract.py` is updated in the same commit rather than preserved.

findings.description: Critical: D2's `answer(...)` builds the console decision with `shared.approval_gate.console_decision(gate, posture, approved, note)`, where D5 defines `posture` as 'the `{disposition, posture_present}` snapshot a parked record carries'. That is true of autopilot's own `pending_gate` in `loop-state.json` (which `runner._console_decision` reads via `pending["posture"]`), but NOT of the supervisor's parked attempt: the parked snapshot is capped at `{kind, reason, gate, deadline, resume_hint}` by both the result schema and `execution.py:416`. So `gate-answer` for a parked child gate has no posture snapshot to pass, and the plan silently assumes one exists.
findings.resolution: In D5, define the posture source for a non-`roadmap_approval` console answer as the router's own prior blocked record in the checkpoint ledger (which carries `disposition` and `posture_present`), not the parked attempt; keep the live-posture snapshot only for an originating `roadmap_approval` answer. Add the case to the task 2.1 test list.

findings.description: Nit: D7 says the router writes the mirror 'through the existing `cycle_state.write_mirror`', but `write_mirror(repo_root, record, *, now)` (cycle_state.py:632-668) is a whole-record replace: it feeds its `record` argument to `_durable_sections`, which returns `pending_gates`, `standing_decisions`, and `back_edge` built solely from that argument. A router that passes only its new `pending_gates` entry therefore erases the existing `back_edge` and every unrelated standing decision. The plan never names the read side of the read-modify-write.
findings.resolution: State in D7 that the router first loads the current durable state (mirror, or `rehydrate`'s selection when the handoff is newer), merges its upsert/removal into all three sections, and passes the merged record to `write_mirror`; add a 'projection preserves back_edge and unrelated standing decisions' case to task 2.1.

findings.description: Nit: D7 fills the `pending_gates` entry's `change_id` for `roadmap_approval` with 'the roadmap's first ready item's change'. `change_id` is required by `$defs.pendingGate` in both supervisor-record schemas and by `_clean_pending_gate`, which drops any entry whose `change_id` fails `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`. A roadmap whose ready set is empty (every item blocked, completed, or without a `change_id`) therefore produces an unrepresentable entry and the blocked roadmap gate vanishes from the digest. The parenthetical 'the `roadmap_ref` convention' also points at a different field: `roadmap_ref` is `<roadmap-id>:ri-NN`, not a change id.
findings.resolution: Define the fallback explicitly in D7 (e.g. the roadmap's first item with a `change_id` regardless of readiness, else refuse to evaluate and report the roadmap as having nothing to approve), fix the `roadmap_ref` parenthetical, and add the empty-ready-set case to the task 2.1 test list.

findings.description: Nit: `ApprovalGate.check_filed(gate, approval_id)` is specified as wrapping `_interpret_status`, but `_interpret_status(gate, gd, status, approval_id, *, notified=True)` needs a `GateDisposition` and a `notified` flag that a later, separate call cannot recover. Two behaviours are left undefined: which posture snapshot supplies `gd` (the posture at file time is gone; the live posture may have flipped, changing `default_action` and hence what `expired` resolves to), and what `notified` is for an approval filed in an earlier process (it decides the fail-closed branch in `_apply_default` when `default_action` is `proceed`). skill-workflow scenario 5 asserts the `approved` / `pending` / unreachable arms but is silent on `expired`.
findings.resolution: Pin in D4 that `check_filed` resolves `gd` from the live posture (consistent with the hot-reload rule) and passes `notified=True` because the approval was demonstrably filed, and add the `expired` arm to the skill-workflow 'Late coordinator answer' scenario and to task 1.4.

findings.description: Nit: the design never pins the `repo_root` the router passes to `build_default_gate`, and the posture a decision is evaluated against depends on it. `ApprovalGate.evaluate` re-reads `TRUST_POSTURE.md` from `repo_root` on every call, and `runner._evaluate_gate` deliberately uses `Path.cwd()` so 'the posture in effect is the one committed on this change's branch'. A supervisor at the shared checkout and a child in an isolated worktree therefore evaluate against different files, and an uncommitted posture edit in the shared checkout is invisible to running children. `resolve_parked` re-evaluating 'against the current posture' will legitimately reach a different answer than the child would have — a design property worth stating, not an accident.
findings.resolution: State in D2 that the router's `repo_root` is the supervisor's repository root (never a child worktree), and add one sentence to D4 step 1 noting that a parked child's gate is re-decided under the supervisor's posture, which is the intended hot-reload seam; mention the commit requirement for posture edits to reach children in the SKILL protocol block (task 3.2).

findings.description: Nit: plan-findings #17 concludes that 'the fingerprint excludes the mirror, so a projection never forces a re-sense', but that only covers the mirror. `_tree_listing` (cycle_state.py:117-145) excludes exactly `LEDGER_PATH` and `MIRROR_PATH`; `openspec/roadmaps/<id>/checkpoint.json` is tracked (`git ls-files` lists it) and is not excluded. Every non-reused router evaluation appends to it, so `compute_fingerprint` changes and the next cycle is never 'unchanged'. Under a `block` posture with no answer the loop still settles (cycle N+1 re-surfaces and writes nothing), but the consequence is unstated and the supervise 'Mirror write preserves unchanged-cycle idempotency' scenario now has a second writer nobody accounted for.
findings.resolution: Either exclude roadmap `checkpoint.json` from `_tree_listing` alongside the ledger and mirror, or state in D7 that a first evaluation deliberately changes the cycle fingerprint and only the reuse / re-surface paths are fingerprint-neutral; add the corresponding assertion to task 2.1.

findings.description: Nit: wp-contracts task 1.1 writes `skills/tests/supervise/test_supervisor_record_schema.py` and task 1.2 adds `Gate.ROADMAP_APPROVAL`, which immediately reddens `test_gate_enum_matches_trust_posture` (that test pins BOTH supervisor-record schemas to `Gate`, at test_supervisor_record_schema.py:52-57). wp-contracts' verification steps run only `skills/shared/tests` and three `tests/autopilot` files, so the package can report green while a suite it owns and edits is red — the failure surfaces only in wp-integration, two packages later.
findings.resolution: Add `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/tests/supervise/test_supervisor_record_schema.py -q` to wp-contracts' verification steps and to the task 1.1 checkpoint command.

findings.description: Optional: D4 step 1.1 maps a parked `pending_gate` to `Gate(parked.gate)` and treats an unknown name as a schema error. `parked.gate` is nullable in `supervised-dispatch-result.schema.json` and in `execution.py:421`'s `_valid_nullable_string` check, and nothing requires it to be set when `kind == "pending_gate"`. `Gate(None)` raises `ValueError` in CPython today but the intent (a null gate on a `pending_gate` park is a malformed child result) is worth naming.
findings.resolution: Add a clause to the 'Unknown parked gate is a schema error' scenario covering a `pending_gate` park with a null `gate`, and mention it in task 2.3.

findings.description: Optional: task 4.3 verifies acceptance outcome 1 with `roadmap_approval: auto` and `pr_creation: auto` and a walk that 'reaches dispatch with no console answer'. The outcome is 'a merged PR' — which also passes the `merge` gate, and the child's gates are evaluated against the posture committed on the child's branch, not the copy task 4.3 edits. As written the fitness function verifies a strictly smaller claim than the outcome it cites.
findings.resolution: Either set every gate to `auto` in the task 4.3 template copy and say the walk stops at dispatch because the child's own gates are ri-06's already-verified surface, or restate task 4.3 as verifying the supervise-side portion of outcome 1 only.

findings.description: Optional: D3 says `resume(...)` calls `require_approval_ref(..., gate=<parked gate or escalate_resume>)`, but `ExecutionAdapter.resume` (execution.py:815-852) pops `attempt["parked"]` as part of the transition. The expected gate must be read from `attempt["parked"]["gate"]` before the field list is stripped, and the reference must be verified before any mutation so a rejected reference leaves the attempt untouched (which the roadmap-orchestration scenario requires).
findings.resolution: Add one sentence to task 2.6 stating that the provenance check runs on the loaded attempt before `_remove_owned_marker` and the field strip.

findings.description: Critical: D5 defines `roadmap_fingerprint` as the sha256 of the sorted `(item_id, change_id, sorted(depends_on))` tuples, which is narrower than the shape the operator actually approved. It omits `external_depends_on` (ri-04 of this very roadmap carries `roadmap-always-on-agent-automation:ri-06`, and `cycle_state.py ready` exists specifically to resolve external edges) and it omits item `status`, so an item flipped to `superseded` or `skipped` — the `_CEDED` statuses `cycle_state` already models, and exactly what `refine-roadmap` produces — leaves the fingerprint unchanged. Under D5's ask-once rule the roadmap then executes under an approval the operator gave for a different scope, with no re-ask. That is the one place in this design where a stale authorization can silently widen what runs unattended.
findings.resolution: Include `external_depends_on` and each item's `status` in the fingerprint tuple (or state explicitly which status transitions are progress and exclude only those), and extend the 'Approved roadmap is not re-asked until its DAG changes' scenario and the task 2.1 test list with a superseded-item and an external-edge case.

findings.description: Nit: task 3.1 says the supervise prose-free test 'mirrors `skills/tests/autopilot/test_prose_free_gates.py`', but that test is not a name scan — it builds a `_GATE_SECTIONS` map from `Gate` to the heading of the section that must carry each gate's protocol block, so a renamed member breaks the map instead of silently dropping a gate. That structure does not transfer: supervise raises only three of the nine gates, so six members have no supervise section to key on. The naive reading in skill-workflow scenario 4 ('every occurrence of a `Gate` name in that file SHALL be inside such a block') also collides with `skills/supervise/SKILL.md:216`, where `merge` appears as an ordinary English word ('PRs awaiting review or merge') and would be a false positive.
findings.resolution: Specify the detection rule in task 3.1 and in skill-workflow scenario 4: scan for backticked or `Gate.`-qualified gate names only, and enumerate which gates supervise is expected to name (`roadmap_approval`, `escalate_resume`, and the parked child's gate) rather than asserting over all nine.

findings.description: D5's exit-code contract for `cycle_state.py gate-check` (3 = proceed, 0 = parked on `posture_block`, 4 = terminal block) is an exact match for `runner.py`'s actual behaviour: `EXIT_NO_PENDING_GATE = 3` on `decision.proceed`, `0` when `session.park` yields `GATE_PENDING`, and `EXIT_GATE_PARKED = 4` for rejected / timeout_default_block / coordinator_unreachable (runner.py:60-67, 171-191). Reusing a verified operator-facing contract instead of inventing a second one is the right call, and the same holds for reusing the checkpoint `gate_decisions` sidecar and `gate-decision.schema.json`, which is `additionalProperties: true` so the new correlation fields are additive as D3 claims.
findings.resolution: No change required.

findings.description: Every MODIFIED requirement in the three spec deltas reproduces all of its live scenarios (supervise: 12/12, 2/2, 3/3; roadmap-orchestration: 3/3, 5/5), with only the five scenarios this change deliberately extends reworded. `openspec validate route-supervise-gates-through-the-approval-gate-service --strict` is green. The Approaches Considered section also correctly rejects reusing `proposal_approval` for the roadmap-altitude decision, which would have collapsed two independently delegable postures into one.
findings.resolution: No change required.
